description: FAILURE scenario — proves the empty-service guard. Path /health/ with prefix "/health/" yields empty string after TrimPrefix. SplitN("", "/", 2) yields [""] — parts[0] is "". The correct return is "". A wrong implementation that returns "health" (treating the prefix itself as a service name) would cause misrouting: the caller would look up "health" in the registry, which does not exist as a service name. The resulting 404 is correct; "health" as a service lookup is not.

injection.mutated_logic: return strings.Split(strings.TrimPrefix(path, "/"), "/")[0] — strips only leading slash, not full prefix
injection.effect: path /health/ with prefix /health/ wrongly yields "health" instead of ""

note: This scenario MUST produce RED when the prefix-strip is replaced with a bare TrimPrefix("/") call. Use as G10/G11 injection fixture for route-service-matcher.
